description:
A $15 million condo in Manhattan or Mumbai costs the same as a 500-year-old stone castle in Europe. Why? Because the money isn't pricing the bricks—it's pricing the dilution.

If you or I walk into a bank asking for a loan double our income, we get laughed out the door. If we can't pay, they impound the car and take the house. But when sovereign governments rack up tens of trillions in debt, nobody evicts the White House. They simply lift the debt cap.

In this deep dive, we break down the 100% Debt Paradox: why total global debt has breached $365 Trillion, why the US spends over $1 Trillion annually just on interest fees, and how the ancient Cantillon Effect ensures that newly minted currency enriches the elite while silently evaporating the purchasing power of your checking account.

From ancient Roman coin melting to John Law’s 1720 fiat bubble, and into the 2020 central bank liquidity pipelines—this is how the machine actually functions. And why the only mathematical defense is to stop swimming and build a boat.
